paper.title: Explore First, Exploit Next: The True Shape of Regret in Bandit Problems

settings.name_in_paper: Stochastic K-armed bandit problem over an arbitrary model D
unmapped: Arm distributions belong to an arbitrary (possibly non-parametric) model D of distributions over R with finite expectation; bounds are expressed via K_inf(nu_a, mu_star, D)
settings.definition_quote:
We consider the simplest case of a stochastic bandit problem, with finitely many arms indexed by $a \in \{1,\ldots,K\}$. Each of these arms is associated with an unknown probability distribution $
u_a$ over~$\R$. We assume that each $
u_a$ has a well-defined expectation and call $\unu = (
u_a)_{a = 1,\ldots,K}$ a bandit problem.

settings.name_in_paper: Bandit model M([0,1]) of all distributions over [0,1] (distribution-free lower bound)
settings.definition_quote: Consider the bandit model $\mathcal{D} = \mathcal{M}\bigl([0,1]\bigr)$ of all probability distributions over $[0,1]$.

settings.name_in_paper: Two-armed Gaussian bandit with known largest expected payoff mu_star
unmapped: mu_star (largest expected payoff) known to the learner, gap unknown

settings.name_in_paper: Two-armed Gaussian bandit with known gap Delta but unknown mu_star
unmapped: gap Delta known to the learner, mu_star unknown

settings.name_in_paper: Sub-Gaussian K-armed bandit with known mu_star
unmapped: mu_star (max expected payoff) known to the learner
settings.definition_quote: We consider the sub-Gaussian framework described in Section~\ref{sec:other-blb} and restrict our attention to the case when $\mu^\star$ is known.

algorithms.name: Algorithm 1: bounded-regret algorithm using knowledge of mu_star

symbols.K_inf: K_inf(nu_a, mu_star, D) = inf KL(nu_a, nu') over nu' in D with E(nu') > mu_star

extra_assumptions: strategy uniformly fast convergent on D: E[N_a(T)] = o(T^alpha) for all alpha in (0,1] and suboptimal a

source.label: th:asympt
source.quote: For all models $\mathcal{D}$, for all uniformly fast convergent strategies $\psi$ on $\cD$, for all bandit problems $\unu$, for all suboptimal arms $a$, \[ \liminf_{T \to \infty} \,\, \frac{\E_{\unu} \! \bigl[ N_{\psi,a}(T) \bigr]}{\ln T} \geq \frac{1}{\Kinf(\nu_a,\mu^\star,\cD)}\,. \]

results.notes: Bound on normalized expected number of pulls of suboptimal arm a / ln T. Re-derivation of Lai-Robbins/Burnetas-Katehakis, though stated for arbitrary models without the extra conditions of Cowan-Katehakis.

extra_assumptions: strategy smarter than the uniform strategy: E[N_{a*}(T)] >= T/K for all optimal arms and all T

source.label: th:2
source.quote: For all models $\cD$, for all strategies $\psi$ that are smarter than the uniform strategy on $\cD$, for all bandit problems~$\unu$, for all arms $a$, for all $T \geq 1$, \[ \E_{\unu} \bigl[ N_{\psi,a}(T) \bigr] \geq \frac{T}{K} \Bigl( 1 - \sqrt{2 T \Kinf(\nu_a,\mu^\star,\cD)} \Bigr)\,. \]

results.notes: Lower bound on expected number of pulls of arm a (not regret directly).

extra_assumptions: strategy smarter than the uniform strategy
results.notes: Initial linear phase for pulls of each arm.

bound.regime: all T >= 1, unless E[N_a(T)] >= T/K (either/or statement)

symbols.KL_a: KL(nu_a, nu_{a*}) between suboptimal arm a and optimal arm a*

extra_assumptions: strategy pairwise symmetric for optimal arms

source.label: th:3
source.quote: For all models $\cD$, for all strategies $\psi$ that are pairwise symmetric for optimal arms on $\cD$, for all bandit problems $\unu$ in $\cD$, for all suboptimal arms $a$ and all optimal arms $a^\star$, for all $T \geq 1$, either $\E_{\unu}[N_{\psi,a}(T)] \geq \frac{T}{K}$ or $\E_{\unu}[\frac{\max\{N_{\psi,a}(T),1\}}{\max\{N_{\psi,a^\star}(T),1\}}] \geq 1 - 2 \sqrt{\frac{2T \, \KL(\nu_a,\nu_{a^\star})}{K}}$.

results.notes: Disjunctive statement; recorded the ratio branch, the alternative being E[N_a(T)] >= T/K. Quantity is the expected ratio of pull counts.

extra_assumptions: strategy pairwise symmetric for optimal arms

symbols.K_max: min over worst arms w of max over optimal arms a* of KL(nu_w, nu_{a*})

extra_assumptions: strategy pairwise symmetric for optimal arms and monotonic

source.label: th:4
source.quote: For all models $\cD$, for all strategies $\psi$ that are pairwise symmetric for optimal arms and monotonic on $\cD$, for all bandit problems $\unu$ in $\cD$, suboptimal arms are collectively sampled at least \sum_{a \not\in \cA^\star(\unu)} \E_{\unu}\bigl[N_{\psi,a}(T)\bigr]\geq T \Bigg(1-\frac{A^\star_{\unu}}{K} -\frac{A^\star_{\unu} \sqrt{ 2T \, \cK^{\max}_{\unu}}}{K}-\frac{2 A^\star_{\unu} T \cK^{\max}_{\unu}}{K}\Bigg)

results.notes: Collective pull-count lower bound; regret follows by multiplying by min suboptimal gap (eq. LBth4).

symbols.K_max: min over worst arms w of max over optimal arms of KL(nu_w, nu_{a*})

extra_assumptions: strategy pairwise symmetric for optimal arms and monotonic

bound.regime: T >= 2 large enough that (ln T)^{-4} < eps_D(mu_star) and a_T, b_T, c_T < 1

symbols.b_T: C_psi * H(nu) * ln T / T, H(nu)=sum over suboptimal arms of 1/Delta_a^2

extra_assumptions: strategy uniformly super-fast convergent: E[N_a(T)] <= C ln T / Delta_a^2
model D well behaved (K_inf locally Lipschitz in second argument)

source.label: th:LBlargeT-NA
source.quote: For all uniformly super-fast convergent strategies $\psi$ on well-behaved models $\mathcal{D}$, for all bandit problems $\unu$ in $\mathcal{D}$, for all suboptimal arms $a$, \E_{\unu}[N_{\psi,a}(T)] \geq \frac{\ln T}{\Kinf(\nu_a,\mu^\star,\cD)} ( 1 - (a_T + b_T + c_T) ) - \frac{\ln 2}{\Kinf(\nu_a,\mu^\star,\cD)}, for all $T \geq 2$ large enough ...

results.notes: Remark: equivalent to ln T/K_inf - O(ln ln T).

bound.regime: epsilon in (0, 1/2); exists a Bernoulli instance

symbols.epsilon: gap parameter of the hard Bernoulli instance (1/2 vs 1/2+epsilon)

source.label: th:distr-free
source.quote: Consider the bandit model $\mathcal{D} = \mathcal{M}\bigl([0,1]\bigr)$ of all probability distributions over $[0,1]$. For all $\varepsilon \in (0,1/2)$, for all strategies $\psi$, there exists a bandit problem $\unu'$ in $\mathcal{M}\bigl([0,1]\bigr)$ such that R_{\psi,\unu',T} \geq T \varepsilon ( 1 - \frac{1}{K} - \frac{1}{2} \sqrt{\frac{T}{K} \ln \frac{1}{1-4\varepsilon^2}} ).

results.notes: Re-proof of Theorem A.2 of Auer et al. (2002); consequence sup regret >= (1/20) min(sqrt(KT), T). Theorem number in appendix as printed may differ.

source.label: eq:distrfree
source.quote: As a consequence, the worst-case regret of any strategy $\psi$ against all bandit problems $\unu$ in $\mathcal{M}\bigl([0,1]\bigr)$ is lower bounded as announced: \sup_{\unu} R_{\psi,\unu,T} \geq ... \geq \frac{1}{20} \min\{ \sqrt{KT}, \, T \}

results.notes: Known result of Auer et al. 2002, re-derived.

symbols.Delta: gap of the two-armed Gaussian instance

extra_assumptions: strategy symmetric: on (N(0,1),N(0,1)) each arm pulled T/2 times in expectation

source.label: th:LB-BPR
source.quote: For all strategies $\psi$ that are symmetric in the sense of~\eqref{eq:sym}, for all $\Delta > 0$, for all $T \geq 1$, \E_{\unu_{\!\Delta}}[N_{\psi,2}(T)] \geq \frac{1}{\Delta^2 + 1/T} and R_{\psi,\unu_{\!\Delta},T} \geq \frac{\Delta}{\Delta^2 + 1/T}.

results.notes: Well-chosen Gaussian instance, mu_star known setting (BPR). Lower bound of order 1/Delta.

symbols.Delta: gap of the two-armed Gaussian instance

source.label: th:LB-BPR
source.quote: In addition, for all strategies $\psi$ and for all $T$ such that $\E_{\unu_{\!\Delta}}[N_{\psi,2}(T)] \geq 1$, ... R_{\psi,\unu_{\!\Delta},T} \geq \min\left\{ \frac{2 (\ln 2) \Delta}{\Delta^2 + 2 \ln(4T)/T}, \,\, \frac{T\Delta}{2} \right\}.

results.notes: No symmetry needed for this part.

bound.regime: all T >= 1; max over the two instances (N(0,1),N(-Delta,1)) and (N(0,1),N(Delta,1))

source.label: th:LB-BPR2
source.quote: We fix $\Delta > 0$ and consider $\unu_1 = ( \cN(0,1), \cN(-\Delta,1) )$ and $\unu_2 = ( \cN(0,1), \cN(\Delta,1) )$. Then, for all strategies $\psi$, for all $T \geq 1$, \max \{ R_{\psi,\unu_1,T}, R_{\psi,\unu_2,T} \} \geq \min \{ \frac{W(T \Delta^2/1.2)}{2 \Delta}, \frac{T\Delta}{2} \}.

results.notes: Re-derivation/improvement of BPR Theorem 6; nonvacuous for small T.

extra_assumptions: strategy symmetric and invariant by translation of the payoffs

source.label: th:LB-BPR2
source.quote: Or, alternatively, for all strategies $\psi$ that are symmetric and invariant by translation of the payoffs, for all $T \geq 1$, R_{\psi,\unu_1,T} = R_{\psi,\unu_2,T} \geq \frac{W(T \Delta^2/1.2)}{2 \Delta}.

source.label: th:finiteRegret:mus:known
source.quote: For all bandit problems $\unu = (\nu_a)_{a = 1,\ldots,K}$ where each distribution $\nu_a$ is sub-Gaussian in the sense of~\eqref{eq:sub-Gaussian}, the regret of the algorithm above is bounded by R_{\unu,T} \leq \sum_{a : \Delta_a > 0} ( \frac{36\ln(17/\Delta_a)}{\Delta_a} + 3\Delta_a ).

results.notes: Bounded (T-independent) regret. Paper says this refinement was already known by BPR authors; algorithm inspired by BPR Algorithm 1.
